tools.name: close_database
tools.title: Close Database
tools.description:
Close a database and terminate its worker process.

Specify *database* when multiple are open. Fails if the DB is
not attached to the current session unless force=True. When other
sessions still use the DB, detaches this session but keeps the
worker alive.

tools.name: save_database
tools.title: Save Database
tools.description:
Save the current database to disk (may take minutes for large DBs).

Specify *database* when multiple are open. Fails if the DB is
not attached to the current session unless force=True. Progress
notifications are sent every 5s during long saves.

tools.name: list_databases
tools.title: List Databases
tools.description: List all open databases with metadata (includes opening/analyzing status).

tools.name: wait_for_analysis
tools.title: Wait for Analysis
tools.description:
Block until database(s) finish opening and optional auto-analysis.

**Single:** pass ``database`` to wait for one DB.
**Multi:** pass ``databases`` list — returns when **at least one**
is ready. Work on the ready one, call again for the rest.

While analysis runs, the backend thread is blocked — tool calls queue.

database.description: Single database ID to wait for.

databases.description: List of database IDs (returns when first is ready).

tools.name: list_targets
tools.title: List Targets
tools.description: List available targets (processors, loaders, languages, etc.).

tools.name: open_database
tools.title: Open Database
tools.description:
Open a binary for analysis with Ghidra.

Returns immediately with ``"opening": true`` — call
wait_for_analysis before using other tools on this database.

An explicit ``database_id`` always opens a worker of its own, so
distinct ids open the *same* file several times and let those
workers analyze it concurrently (up to the configured maximum).
Without ``database_id``, re-opening the same file returns the
existing worker.

**Multiple binaries:** use a separate subagent per binary.

**force_new=True** is destructive: deletes existing Ghidra
project and all prior analysis.

database_id.description:
Custom ID (must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}).
Reusing an id that is already open is rejected; a new id
for an already-open path opens an additional worker.

force_new.description:
Delete existing project and start fresh. With no
database_id it replaces the path's worker; it does not by
itself create a second one.

language.description:
Ghidra language ID (e.g. ``x86:LE:64:default``,
      ``ARM:LE:32:v8``). Auto-detected when omitted.
      Use list_targets to see options.

compiler_spec.description:
Ghidra compiler spec (e.g. ``gcc``,
           ``windows``). Auto-detected when omitted.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description:
Search hidden tools by regex (pinned tools excluded; use ``.*`` for all).

Returns one-line signatures by default. Use ``detail="detailed"``
for parameter schemas, or follow up with ``get_schema(tools=[...])``.

Hidden tools must be called via **call**, **batch**, or **execute**
— direct calls will fail because they are not in the client tool list.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against tool names, descriptions, and tags

detail.description: 'brief' (default) for a one-line signature + summary per tool, 'detailed' for parameter schemas as markdown, 'full' for complete JSON schemas

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description:
Get parameter schemas for specific tools by name (pinned and hidden).

Use after search_tools or before execute/batch to check parameter
types and return shapes. Pass ``detail="full"`` for complete JSON schemas.

Hidden tools must be called via **call**, **batch**, or **execute**
— direct calls will fail because they are not in the client tool list.
Tool names to get schemas for.

detail.description: 'brief' for a one-line signature + summary per tool, 'detailed' for parameter schemas as markdown (default), 'full' for complete JSON schemas

tools.name: execute
tools.description:
Run Python code that chains tool calls. Use `await invoke(name, params)` to call tools; use `return` to produce output.

`database` is auto-injected into every `invoke` — omit it from params. Override per-call with explicit `database` for cross-database work.

## When NOT to use execute

- **Single tool call** → use the **call** meta-tool (or the direct tool if pinned).
- **N independent calls** → use `batch` (lower overhead, per-item errors).
  → Otherwise, use the **batch** meta-tool for sequential multi-tool
    execution with per-item error collection and progress reporting.
- Check if a tool has a built-in batch parameter first (e.g. get_strings `filters=[...]`).

## When to use execute

**Multi-step pipelines** — chaining one tool's output into another:
```
decomp = await invoke("decompile_function", {"address": "0x1234"})
addrs = re.findall(r'sub_([0-9A-Fa-f]+)', decomp["pseudocode"])
xrefs = [await invoke("get_xrefs_to", {"address": f"0x{a}"}) for a in addrs]
return {"decomp": decomp, "xrefs": xrefs}
```

**Cross-database parallel queries** — use asyncio.gather with explicit `database` params. Same-database calls are serialized by the worker.

## Reference

- **Blocked tools:** open_database, close_database, wait_for_analysis, list_targets, and meta-tools (search_tools, get_schema, execute, batch, call) must be called directly. save_database and list_databases are allowed.
- **Addresses** are strings: "0x401000", "4010a0", or symbol names.
- **filter_pattern** is Python regex — use `re.escape()` for literals.
- **Available imports:** asyncio, collections, functools, itertools, json, math, operator, re, struct, typing. No FS/network I/O.
- **Paginated results** have `items`, `total`, `offset`, `limit`, `has_more` — always check `has_more`.
- Use `get_schema(tools=[...])` to look up parameter names and types.
- **Return only what you need** — filter before returning to save context.

code.description: Python async code to execute tool calls via invoke(name, arguments)

database.description: Database to target (stem ID from open_database). Available as `database` variable in code and auto-injected into invoke params. Individual calls can override by passing `database` explicitly.

tools.name: batch
tools.description:
Run 2+ independent tool calls in a single request with per-item error collection.

Preferred over `execute` for independent calls (no sandbox overhead).
Examples: decompile/disassemble N functions, rename N symbols, set N
comments, fetch N xrefs.

Use `execute` only when chaining one tool's output into another.

`database` is auto-injected into each operation — omit from params.
Override per-operation with explicit `database` for cross-DB work.

operations.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially (max 50).

items.description: A single operation in a batch request.

database.description: Database to target (stem ID from open_database). Auto-injected into each operation's params. Individual operations can override by including `database` in their params.

stop_on_error.description: Stop on first error instead of continuing.

items.description: Result of one operation in a batch.

result.description: Tool result on success, null on error.
result.title: Result

error.description: Error message if this item failed.

cancelled.description: Whether batch stopped before completing all operations (stop_on_error or client cancellation).

tools.name: call
tools.description:
Call any tool by name, including hidden tools not in the client tool list.

Use for single hidden-tool calls. For multiple calls, prefer **batch**.

arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the tool.

database.description: Database to target (stem ID from open_database). Auto-injected into arguments unless already present.
